hero_subtitle: The Iconic Blue Pearl of Morocco Nested in the Scenic Rif Mountains.

overview.title: Welcome to the Blue Pearl
overview.p1: Chefchaouen is world-famous for its striking palette of blue-washed buildings tucked into the dramatic peaks of the Rif Mountains. Founded in 1471 as a fortress, this tranquil mountain town offers a peaceful retreat from Morocco's bustling imperial cities.
overview.p2: Wander through winding cobblestone alleys, relax in vibrant squares with mint tea, watch the sunset over the valley from the Spanish Mosque, or trek through the lush natural trails of Talassemtane National Park.

places.title: Top Places to Visit in Chefchaouen
places.subtitle: Iconic blue alleyways, historic kasbahs, and scenic mountain viewpoints.

outa.title: Place Outa el Hammam
outa.desc: The vibrant central square lined with outdoor cafés, dominated by the red-walled Kasbah and Grand Mosque.

kasbah.title: Chefchaouen Kasbah
kasbah.desc: A 15th-century fortress featuring lush Andalusian gardens, an ethnographic museum, and panoramic tower views.

raselmaa.title: Ras El Maa Spring
raselmaa.desc: Fresh mountain water spring outside the east medina gate where locals gather and wash rugs.

mosquee.title: Spanish Mosque (Bouzafar)
mosquee.desc: A hilltop mosque offering the ultimate sunset view over the entire blue medina and surrounding valley.

akchour.title: Akchour Waterfalls & God's Bridge
akchour.desc: Stunning river hikes, emerald pools, and natural rock arches in Talassemtane National Park.

haouta.title: Place El Haouta
haouta.desc: A peaceful square with a zellige fountain, perfect for mint tea away from the busy alleys.

babelain.title: Bab El Ain & Souks
babelain.desc: The main southern entrance to the medina leading to artisan workshops and local markets.

souika.title: Al Souika District
souika.desc: The oldest residential area featuring blue-washed cobblestone alleyways and carved doorways.

talassemtane.title: Talassemtane National Park
talassemtane.desc: Protected nature reserve with fir forests, dramatic peaks, and scenic hiking trails.

itinerary.title: Suggested 3-Day Itinerary
itinerary.subtitle: A relaxed schedule to capture the best photography spots and mountain landscapes.

day1.title: Exploring the Blue Medina & Sunset View
day1.desc: Stroll through the blue alleys, visit the Kasbah, enjoy tea at Place Outa el Hammam, and hike up to the Spanish Mosque for sunset.

day2.title: Akchour Waterfalls & Local Flavors
day2.desc: Take a morning grand taxi to Akchour for a scenic river hike, return for a traditional goat cheese tasting and rooftop dinner.

day3.title: Artisans, Relax & Ras El Maa
day3.desc: Walk along the Ras El Maa spring, observe local weavers, taste fresh mountain goat cheese, and shop for handmade products.
day3.duration: Half Day • Ras El Maa & Souks

eat.title: Best Restaurants & Cafés
eat.subtitle: Authentic Northern Moroccan dishes, goat cheese, and rooftop views

ssour.title: Bab Ssour
ssour.desc: Cozy multi-story restaurant serving home-cooked Tagines, fresh salads, and local specialties.

sofia.title: Restaurant Sofia
sofia.desc: Family-run eatery known for heartwarming pastillas, tajines, and friendly hospitality.

clock.title: Café Clock Chefchaouen
clock.desc: Vibrant cultural hub offering camel burgers, cooking classes, storytelling, and panoramic rooftop views.

morisco.title: Restaurant Morisco
morisco.desc: Prime spot on the main square for mint tea, breakfast, and people-watching.

aladdin.title: Restaurant Aladdin
aladdin.desc: Arabo-Andalusian palace offering panoramic Kasbah views from three rooftop terraces.

mandala.title: Mandala Pizzeria
mandala.desc: Wood-fired pizzas featuring local mountain goat cheese and fresh homemade pasta.

triana.title: Restaurant Triana
triana.desc: Charming riverside eatery blending refined Moroccan dishes with Spanish influences.

transport.title: Getting Here & Around
transport.desc: Reach Chefchaouen via CTM bus or private driver from Tangier (2h) or Fez (4h). The medina is car-free and best explored on foot.

shoes.title: Steep Alleyways & Shoes
shoes.desc: Wear comfortable walking shoes with good grip — the cobblestone steps and blue streets can be steep and slippery.

photo.title: Photography Etiquette
photo.desc: Always ask permission before taking close-up photos of locals, especially elders and children in the medina.

cash.title: Cash & ATMs
cash.desc: Most small shops, cafés, and local Dars only accept cash (Moroccan Dirham MAD). ATMs are available near Place Outa el Hammam.

daytrips.title: Best Day Trips from Chefchaouen
daytrips.subtitle: Discover waterfalls, national parks, and coastal mountain roads nearby.

akchour.title: Akchour Waterfalls & Bridge
akchour.desc: Emerald pools, river hikes, and the natural rock arch of God's Bridge (45 min drive).

talassemtane.title: Talassemtane National Park
talassemtane.desc: Trekking trails through fir forests, mountain peaks, and remote Rif villages.

tetouan.title: Tetouan Medina
tetouan.desc: UNESCO-listed Andalusian medina with rich artisan heritage (1h30 drive).

ouedlaou.title: Mediterranean Coast (Oued Laou)
ouedlaou.desc: Pebble beaches and turquoise waters of the Mediterranean coast (1h15 drive).

tanger.title: Tangier - Gateway to Africa
tanger.desc: Combine your journey with the legendary coastal city on the Strait of Gibraltar (2h15 drive).

q1.question: How many days should I spend in Chefchaouen?
q1.answer: 2 to 3 days is ideal to wander the medina, catch the sunset at the Spanish Mosque, and take a day trip to the Akchour waterfalls.

q2.question: Is Chefchaouen easy to reach by train?
q2.answer: No, Chefchaouen has no train station. The easiest options are CTM buses, grand taxis, or private transfers from Tangier, Tetouan, or Fez.

q3.question: Why is Chefchaouen painted blue?
q3.answer: Several theories exist: introduced by Jewish refugees in the 1930s symbolizing heaven, kept as a natural mosquito repellent, or maintained to keep homes cool and attract visitors.

q4.question: Are cards accepted in Chefchaouen?
q4.answer: Most small shops, cafés, and local Dars only accept cash (Moroccan Dirham MAD). ATMs are available near Place Outa el Hammam.

detailed_itinerary.day1_m: Morning — Place Outa el Hammam & the Kasbah
detailed_itinerary.day1_md: Start in the main square, visit the Kasbah and its gardens, then wander into the blue alleys while the light is soft and the streets are quiet.
detailed_itinerary.day1_a: Afternoon — Lost in the Blue Alleys
detailed_itinerary.day1_ad: Take your time in the medina’s lanes, stopping at small shops and cafés. Enjoy mint tea on the square and keep the camera ready for every corner.
detailed_itinerary.day1_e: Evening — Sunset at the Spanish Mosque
detailed_itinerary.day1_ed: Hike up to the Spanish Mosque for panoramic views over the blue rooftops at golden hour, then walk back down for dinner in the medina.
detailed_itinerary.day2_md: Take an early grand taxi to Akchour for a scenic river walk through Talassemtane National Park, with the Little Waterfall or the God’s Bridge trail if you have the energy.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ad: Head back to town in the afternoon and taste the region’s famous goat cheese, along with fresh bread and olives from a local vendor.
detailed_itinerary.day2_ed: Finish the day with a traditional dinner on a rooftop terrace overlooking the medina lights.
detailed_itinerary.day3_md: Walk to the Ras El Maa spring at the edge of the medina, where locals gather, wash and relax by the water.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ad: Visit local weavers and craft shops to see woven blankets, wool goods and handmade products being made, and buy directly from the artisans.
detailed_itinerary.day3_ed: Enjoy a last mint tea in the square before heading on to your next destination.
